method: Preserved the retained historical summary log and a redacted note of the ignored source hash, modification times, and scorer behavior. Ran the offline lesson/evidence checks and candidate-rule fixtures. Compared current Anthropic API claims with linked official docs. No provider request or historical model run was replayed.

observations.trace: The lesson’s historical A score is not recoverable: prose says 7/7, log says 6/7, and the displayed failure row has identical expected and visible actual dates. B and control are only unverified 4/4 summaries. Current script scoring appends a truncation marker but still uses expected-in-output substring matching; its later mtime means it cannot be established as the run version. Effect is unknown.

limitations: No raw per-request model responses, stop reasons, usage, request IDs, endpoint/model fingerprint, sample-to-response mapping, scorer version, or aggregation artifact is retained.
The archived run log and the current ignored script may represent different versions; no historical script hash ties them together.
No new provider requests were made and the old run was not replayed.
Offline fixtures verify lesson wording and the candidate-rule helper behavior only; they do not measure whether any distilled rule improves a model or production system.
Anthropic stop-reason semantics are scoped to the current Anthropic Messages API documentation; compatible endpoints require independent contract checks.

The historical log is a short summary, not the raw provider response; the source-facts note records the current ignored script hash and observed scorer behavior but cannot prove it produced the archived run.
